territorial_scope.description: Applies to Medicare payment for covered outpatient department services under Title XVIII of the Social Security Act, a federal program.

evidence.quote: Section 1833(t) of the Social Security Act (42 U.S.C. 1395l(t)) is amended

agora_applications: Medicine, life sciences and public health

summary.short: Amends Social Security Act §1833(t) so that FDA-cleared algorithm-based healthcare services furnished in hospital outpatient departments from January 1, 2026 are assigned to new technology ambulatory payment classifications based on manufacturer-submitted costs, and directs HHS to apply a software-as-a-service payment policy from January 1, 2023.
summary.long: The Health Tech Investment Act amends Section 1833(t) of the Social Security Act to add a special rule for algorithm-based healthcare services, defined as services delivered through an FDA-cleared or approved device that uses artificial intelligence, machine learning or similar software to yield clinical outputs for use by a physician or practitioner in screening, detection, diagnosis or treatment. For covered outpatient department services furnished on or after January 1, 2026, the Secretary must ensure that qualifying services are assigned to a new technology ambulatory payment classification based on costs submitted by the manufacturer, must adjust that classification as necessary, and may not remove a service from it until adequate claims data exists, and in no case before the service has received payment under the classification for at least five years. The Secretary must also adjust eligibility criteria so that distinct adjunctive algorithm-based services can qualify. Section 2(b) directs the Secretary to apply the outpatient payment policy for software as a service, described in a November 23, 2022 final rule, to services provided on or after January 1, 2023. The text contains no enforcement or penalty provisions.

relations.note: Sec. 2(a) amends section 1833(t) of the Social Security Act by adding a new paragraph (16)(H) and changing paragraph (2)(E). The target is not in the registry.

notes: Bill as introduced; no enacted text. Relations come only from references in this bill's text. No target is in the registry, so target_instrument_id is an empty string. Sec. 2(b) sets an effective date of January 1, 2023, which is earlier than the bill's introduction; Sec. 2(a) applies from January 1, 2026 for covered OPD services. Sec. 2(b)'s payment policy is identified only by reference to the 2022 final rule, so its content is not coded. The 2001 rule's title says 'Calendar Year 2002' but the text gives its publication date as November 30, 2001; this is reproduced as written.
